findings.title: `.title { float: left; }` rule removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous `.title { float: left; }` rule inside `.contents` was deleted and not replaced by any flex-related property (no explicit `order`, `flex`, or alignment rule for `.title`). Since `.contents` is now `display:flex`, the `.title` element becomes a flex item relying entirely on default flex behavior, which can change its sizing/position compared to the previous floated layout (e.g. width calculation, wrapping behavior). This looks like an accidental omission rather than an intentional simplification and risks visually breaking the header title/logo layout.

findings.title: Float-based child layout left in place after converting `.small-action` to flexbox
findings.body: `.small-action` was converted to `display: flex` (lines 264-265), but its children `.topic-avatar` (line 270, `float: left`) and `button` (line 309, `float: right`) still rely on `float` for positioning. The CSS flexbox spec explicitly makes `float` a no-op on flex items, so these floats no longer have any effect. As a result the avatar is no longer guaranteed to sit to the left and the trailing button is no longer pushed to the right — the three children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, `button`) will instead lay out in normal flex row order with no explicit `order`/`margin-left:auto` compensation, which changes the visual layout from what was previously intended.

findings.title: `.small-action-desc` left padding drastically reduced, likely causing overlap with the icon
findings.body: `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` was changed to `padding: 0 1.5%;`. The original 4em left padding was almost certainly reserved to make room for the floated `.topic-avatar` icon (45px wide, set via `.topic-avatar i { width: 45px; }`). With the new padding of only 1.5%, combined with floats no longer applying inside the new flex container (see related finding), the description text/icon are likely to overlap or be misaligned, which is a visible regression.

findings.title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` without a compensating rule
findings.body: The previous nested rule setting `margin-top: 5px` on `.badge-wrapper.bullet` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` was deleted with no replacement. This was presumably used to vertically align the bullet badge within the line; removing it without adding any corresponding alignment (e.g. via flex `align-items`) risks a vertical misalignment regression for bullet-style category badges in the extra-info area.

findings.title: `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` with no verified flex parent
findings.body: The CSS `order` property only has an effect when the element is a direct child of a `display:flex` (or similar) container. From the shown file there is no indication that the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` is a flex container; if it isn't, this `order` declaration is dead code that has no visual effect, and if it is intended to be meaningful, the PR should verify/establish the flex container on the parent to avoid silently non-functional CSS.

findings.title: Removed `padding-top: 4px` from `.small-action-desc > p` without explanation
findings.body: The `padding-top: 4px` previously applied to the first-level paragraph inside `.small-action-desc` was removed. Combined with the other spacing changes in this same selector block, this reduces vertical spacing that may have been needed for readability/alignment of the small-action description text, and there is no indication this was deliberate given the PR description does not explain the rationale.
